posts.author: JohnDoeGames
posts.body:
STORY:
Farmboy wakes up early in the morning, because well, farmers wake up early. And Farmboy is going to be a farmer just like his dad.
End of story...
GAMEPLAY:
If not for story, what should you play this game for? Well, to farm! You plant fruits and vegetables, then harvest them, and then you plant more. You bake what you grow into delicious feasts, which you sell for money.
Buy farm animals for their eggs, milk and meat... And their poop! Use the poop as fertilizer and the other items as ingredients.
And if that isn't farmy enough, you can get busy fishing for more ingredients. You also get to fish for the extremely rare Golden Carp. Those can be used as currency to buy more animals and pets.
PLAY THE GAME:
You can play the game on my itchio account. It was posted there as my submission to the RPG Maker 2025 game jam, and can be played in the browser, or downloaded for windows.
Farmboy by JohnDoeNews
Farming simulator made for RPG Maker 2025 Game Jam
johndoenews.itch.io
OTHER COMMENTS:
This game is created to be 100% child friendly. You can safely play this with your kids.
CREDTITS:
Game by: JohnDoeNews
Engine: RPG Maker MV
Music by: ElvGames & Pegonthetrack
Graphics by: FinalBossBlues
Plugins by: OcRam and yanfly

posts.author: JohnDoeGames
posts.body:
See... you tell me what you expect of a farm simulator.... but the fact that you play a farm simulator made with RPG maker, that is the unexpected part.
it says in the rules that innovative mechanics are according to theme. I made 20 different crops that can grow from a single event, have 4 growth stages each with their own requirements. I made a Fishing system that respawns over time. And it all happens on real time. It updates while you watch.
That might be expected of farm sims, but it is unexpected for RPG maker games. And
that
was the assignment. That it has exactly what you expect from a farming sim, is what I aimed for.
Thanks for trying out my game. I'm happy to read you liked it and you've kept playing for 2 hours, which should be more than enough to unlock the whole farm, so I guess you got invested in fishing?
I did see the feedback about the waiting time for items. I will think about some kind of indicator. But this means I need to recreate the whole animal system, since that timer is calculated when you interact with it. Not in real time like the fishing ponds and the crops.

So I went for a farming system, and made it as well as I could imagine. I'd love to make something in a farming game that you wouldn't expect there, but I honestly think it would be a bad choice.
If I put in aliens that mutate my sheep, then no-one would see that coming... But it doesn't really fit inside a farming simulator. If I would make a brutal slaughter ritual to gain meat, no-one would expect that, but that isn't very child friendly.

Of course I hope they will find this unexpected enough, though.

posts.author: JohnDoeGames
posts.body:
Well, play it safe... Maybe is some way. The thing is, I didn't expect to join. I have a full time job and often work weekends and evenings as well. So I came up with something last minute. I had to think of something I could create fast. So you could say I played it safe with the time limit.
Because that is the thing. I did create a lot, but to create those systems, I often worked on those for weeks in a row, 120 hours a week. When I am on a roll, I don't sleep until the job is done. But I can't do that now, since I have a job to go to and rent to pay and such.
What I could have done, was re-use one of the old mechanics to create a new game. If I understood the rules right, that would be allowed, but I would have felt like a cheater if I used my card game mechanics (which is years of progress) in a game jam with a 1 month time limit.
However, I found I had much more time than I needed, so I had many hours to test the systems and to polish it, even after I submitted the game. (I've asked, judges won't check the games will the deadline had passed) Like, I've added fishing quests and those indicators when crops need attention. And I balanced the cooldown periods. I hope that will make it a bit more outstanding.
But if the judges find it not innovative enough, then so be it. I had a blast creating this game, and I honestly think this is a good, finished products. And (something that wasn't the assignment, but I took this one very seriously) it is all 100% child friendly. I think making this was a good thing, even if I don't win.
As long as I get the badge, I am happy.
Hahaha.
